classification.difficultyReason: Follow supplied midpoint construction steps for a half-size image, then check corresponding lengths and angles.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows a rectangle $ABCD$ and a point $O$. Copy or trace the diagram into your exercise book.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 9A Question 2, rectangle above part a
spec.description: Unshaded upright rectangle with O well to its left, level with its centre. Internal drawing coordinates reproduce relative placement and are not student-visible givens.
spec.mathematics: A top left, B top right, C bottom right, D bottom left; no dimensions, coordinates or additional marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original rectangle and centre are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Now apply an enlargement with centre $O$ and factor $\frac12$ using these steps:

children.label: i
children.prompt: Join $OA$ and mark the midpoint $A'$ of $OA$.

answer.worked: Draw $OA$ and mark $A'$ on it so that $OA'=A'A=\frac12 OA$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Join $OB$ and mark the midpoint $B'$ of $OB$.

answer.worked: Draw $OB$ and mark $B'$ on it so that $OB'=B'B=\frac12 OB$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Join $OC$ and mark the midpoint $C'$ of $OC$.

answer.worked: Draw $OC$ and mark $C'$ on it so that $OC'=C'C=\frac12 OC$.

children.label: iv
children.prompt: Join $OD$ and mark the midpoint $D'$ of $OD$.

answer.short: $D'$ is the midpoint of $OD$; the image is rectangle $A'B'C'D'$.
answer.worked: Draw $OD$ and mark $D'$ on it so that $OD'=D'D=\frac12 OD$. Join $A'$, $B'$, $C'$ and $D'$ in order to complete the image.

spec.description: Complete construction with the original rectangle, four centre-to-vertex segments and the midpoint image.
spec.mathematics: Each primed vertex is the midpoint of its corresponding segment from O. A′B′C′D′ is the factor-1/2 image of ABCD.
spec.answerVisibility: Construction guides and the blue image appear only in answers.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use compasses to verify that each side length of $A'B'C'D'$ is half the corresponding side length of $ABCD$.

answer.worked:
Set the compasses to each image side in turn. Transferring that span twice along the corresponding original side reaches its other endpoint, confirming
$$\begin{aligned}A'B'&=\tfrac12 AB\\B'C'&=\tfrac12 BC\\C'D'&=\tfrac12 CD\\D'A'&=\tfrac12 DA.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use a protractor to verify that each angle of $A'B'C'D'$ is a right angle, matching the angles of $ABCD$.

answer.short: All four image angles are $90^\circ$, matching the corresponding original angles.
answer.worked: Measure each interior angle of $A'B'C'D'$ with a protractor. Each measures $90^\circ$, within drawing and measurement accuracy. These match the four right angles of rectangle $ABCD$, as enlargement preserves angles.
